question: A person travels by a motorcycle to a place at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns at an average speed of 30 km/h. Find his average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal forward and return distances, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Here, forward speed (S₁) = 60 km/h and return speed (S₂) = 30 km/h.

Average Speed = (2 × 60 × 30) ÷ (60 + 30)

Average Speed = 3600 ÷ 90 = 40 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed during forward journey = 60 km/h

Speed during return journey = 30 km/h

Let the one-way distance between the starting point and the place be D km.

 
 
 Start
 Destination
 
• 
 Distance = D km
 
• 
 

 Speed = 60 km/h
 
• 
 

 Speed = 30 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = Forward Distance + Return Distance = D + D = 2D km

⇒ Time for forward journey = D ÷ 60 hours

⇒ Time for return journey = D ÷ 30 hours

⇒ Total Time = (D ÷ 60) + (D ÷ 30)

⇒ Total Time = (D + 2D) ÷ 60 = 3D ÷ 60 = D ÷ 20 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (D ÷ 20)

⇒ Average Speed = 2D × (20 ÷ D)

⇒ Average Speed = 40 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a person covers three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z respectively, the average speed is given by the formula: 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Unit Conversion Tricks

To quickly convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18. Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is S₁ − S₂. When moving in opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.
